sources.label: Scaling Latent Reasoning via Looped Language Models, arXiv:2510.25741

beats.narration: Ooro runs the same layers over and over. ByteDance says a two point six billion version matches models up to twelve billion. What's being counted?
beats.narration_text: Ouro-2.6B: (1) explain how a looped language model reuses its layers, (2) explain the learned early-exit gate, (3) compute stored parameters vs per-token compute at 4 recurrent steps — and tell me whether 'matches 12B models' is a fair comparison.

props.command: Ouro-2.6B: (1) explain how a looped language model reuses its layers, (2) explain the learned early-exit gate, (3) compute stored parameters vs per-token compute at 4 recurrent steps — and tell me whether 'matches 12B models' is a fair comparison.
output: LOOP   48 layers × up to 4 recurrent steps
EXIT   a learned gate decides when to stop

beats.narration: Depth from repetition, not more weights. The loop, the exit gate, the count, and whether the comparison is fair.
beats.narration_text: Depth from repetition, not more weights. The loop, the exit gate, the count, and whether the comparison is fair.

props.title: Ouro, Smarter by Repeating?
thesis: Ouro-1.4B and Ouro-2.6B, trained on 7.7T tokens, run one layer stack
up to four times — depth from repetition, not from more stored weights.

roadmap.label: The loop
roadmap.body: 48 layers, the same weights, up to 4 steps.

beats.narration: One stack of forty-eight layers runs again and again with the same weights, up to four times. After each step, a learned gate asks if it's done.
beats.narration_text: One stack of forty-eight layers runs again and again with the same weights, up to four times. After each step, a learned gate asks if it's done.

props.heading: The loop, step by step

moves.label: LOOP
moves.detail: One 48-layer stack runs, then runs again with the same weights.

moves.label: STEPS
moves.detail: Up to 4 recurrent steps refine the same hidden state.

moves.label: EXIT
moves.detail: After each step a learned gate asks: done yet? Easy inputs stop early.

moves.label: TRAIN
moves.detail: An entropy-regularized objective learns how deep each input goes.

props.keepNote: Row 3 is the trick: depth becomes a per-input decision, not a fixed size.

beats.narration: Now count. Two point six billion parameters stored. But at four steps, each token passes through a hundred ninety-two layer applications: roughly a ten billion parameter dense model's compute. Small to store, not small to run.
beats.narration_text: Now count. Two point six billion parameters stored. But at four steps, each token passes through a hundred ninety-two layer applications: roughly a ten billion parameter dense model's compute. Small to store, not small to run.

props.spark: Small to store. Not small to run.
props.heading: Ouro-2.6B — stored vs computed
props.exception: Computed: 4 × 2.47B looped layers + 0.20B embeddings and head, run once ≈ 10.1B per token.
props.source: Computed from config.json (48 layers, total_ut_steps 4, vocab 49,152) + the 2.67B checkpoint; 12B: arXiv:2510.25741

beats.narration: So is matching twelve billion fair? Its own model card says three to four billion. On memory, yes. On compute, closer than it sounds: four passes cost about four times one.
beats.narration_text: So is matching twelve billion fair? Its own model card says three to four billion. On memory, yes. On compute, closer than it sounds: four passes cost about four times one.

props.heading: Is “matches 12B” fair?

moves.label: CLAIM
moves.detail: Abstract: 1.4B and 2.6B “match the results of up to 12B”; the 2.6B card says 3–4B.

moves.label: COMPUTE
moves.detail: Softer: 4 steps ≈ 4 passes per token, much closer to the 12B side.

moves.label: WHY
moves.detail: The gain is “knowledge manipulation”, not more knowledge capacity.

props.keepNote: Fair on memory. Softer on compute. Compare looped models per FLOP, not per parameter.

beats.narration: Smarter by repeating? Partly. The loop buys reasoning steps without more weights, but every step costs compute and adds no knowledge. Compare looped models on compute, not size.
beats.narration_text: Smarter by repeating? Partly. The loop buys reasoning steps without more weights, but every step costs compute and adds no knowledge. Compare looped models on compute, not size.

artifactLines: Mechanism: one 48-layer stack, run up to 4 times, with a learned exit gate.
Count: 2.6B stored, ~4 passes of compute per token at full depth.
Claim: matches up to 12B models — fair on memory, softer on compute.
Looping adds reasoning steps, not stored knowledge (the paper's own finding).
props.sourceNote: ByteDance Seed et al., arXiv:2510.25741 · ByteDance/Ouro-2.6B config.json

beats.narration: Your turn. Force the model to one, two, three and four steps. If extra passes help math but not trivia, you've reproduced the paper's main claim.
beats.narration_text: Run Ouro-1.4B with depth forced to 1, 2, 3 and 4 recurrent steps. On 50 math word problems and 50 trivia questions, report accuracy and tokens per second at each depth. Where do extra passes help — reasoning, recall, or neither?

props.command: Run Ouro-1.4B with depth forced to 1, 2, 3 and 4 recurrent steps. On 50 math word problems and 50 trivia questions, report accuracy and tokens per second at each depth. Where do extra passes help — reasoning, recall, or neither?
output: GOOD   reasoning climbs with steps · recall flat
FLAG   no change → the loop isn't doing much
